source.title: The speed of parietal theta frequency drives visuospatial working memory capacity

confidence_rationale: A causal (not merely correlational) manipulation: transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) at 4 Hz vs. 7 Hz over parietal cortex CHANGES visuospatial working-memory capacity (K-values) in opposite directions, lateralized to the stimulated hemisphere's contralateral visual field. This is the strongest available direct evidence in this pull that a rhythm/frequency parameter can SET item capacity rather than merely correlating with a separately-determined count -- the exact causal direction MECH-522 needs (coupling constant as setter, not readout). Confidence is capped because the manipulated frequency band and mechanism (theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling via cortical rhythms) is a single GLOBAL parietal rhythm setting ONE capacity number, not a heterogeneous field acting differently per stream -- MECH-522's more specific and more distinctive claim.
failure_signatures: If working-memory item capacity were fixed by a slot-count mechanism independent of oscillatory dynamics, externally imposing a different theta frequency via tACS should not change K-values at all -- but 4-Hz tACS significantly enhanced K-values (and accuracy) relative to sham while 7-Hz tACS significantly reduced them (Cohen's d 0.44-0.57), which is inconsistent with a fixed, rhythm-independent capacity and consistent with the rhythm ITSELF acting as (or directly setting) the capacity-determining parameter.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Transcranial alternating current stimulation at slow theta (4 Hz) over parietal cortex causally enhances visuospatial working memory capacity (higher K-values, better accuracy) relative to sham, while fast theta (7 Hz) causally reduces it, with effects lateralized to the visual hemifield contralateral to stimulation. The authors interpret this via theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling: slower theta cycles nest more gamma subcycles, each subcycle carrying one item, so slower theta mechanically permits a higher item count.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-522 proposes that ephaptic field strength is the COUPLING CONSTANT of a settling competition that SETS slot occupancy, rather than a quantity that is measured and counted after the fact. This paper supplies the cleanest available causal-manipulation evidence for that direction of causality in any oscillatory system: externally imposing a different rhythm parameter (frequency) changes the realized item count in the SAME direction the coupling-constant framing predicts (slower rhythm -> more nested capacity). It is the strongest 'field/coupling sets count, rather than count being separately measured then correlated with field properties' evidence found in this pull.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Two gaps against MECH-522's more specific claim. First, this is a single GLOBAL parietal theta rhythm setting ONE scalar capacity number for the whole task -- not a field with a per-stream coherence length/frequency giving HETEROGENEOUS, simultaneously-different domain counts across streams, which is MECH-522's more distinctive claim (the part that goes beyond Lisman & Jensen's already-on-file theta-gamma account). It is evidence for 'a rhythm parameter can causally set capacity,' not evidence for 'the setting is natively heterogeneous across streams.' Second, this is synaptic/oscillatory (tACS entrains ongoing neural oscillations via the same currents that drive spiking), not specifically an EPHAPTIC (non-synaptic extracellular field) mechanism -- MECH-522's specific bet on ephaptic coupling as opposed to any generic neuromodulatory or rhythmic gate is not tested here.
mapping.source_context: 32 healthy adult participants (16 per electrode-montage group); within-subject tACS at 4 Hz, 7 Hz, and sham over parietal cortex during a visuospatial delayed match-to-sample task (memory loads of 4, 5, 6 colored squares, lateralized presentation); K-value (Cowan's K, an estimate of items successfully held in working memory) as the outcome measure.

confidence_components.notes: Peer-reviewed, causal (stimulation) design with a reasonable sample (n=32) and a clean double-dissociation (opposite-direction effects at two frequencies, both relative to sham, both lateralized as predicted). Mapping fidelity capped by the single-global-rhythm vs. heterogeneous-per-stream-field gap described above; transfer risk moderate (human tACS/cortical rhythms to REE's engineered heartbeat/ephaptic-analog substrate, which MECH-089/V3-EXQ-725a already partially address in an on-file, unresolved way).
